title: HiGPT: Heterogeneous Graph Language Model

problem.claim: Heterogeneous graph models need to adapt to downstream tasks under distribution shifts in node token sets and relation-type heterogeneity.

gap.claim: Existing frameworks have limited generalization across diverse heterogeneous graph datasets because they commonly pre-train and fine-tune on the same dataset.

contributions.claim: HiGPT is a general large graph model using a heterogeneous graph instruction-tuning paradigm.
An in-context heterogeneous graph tokenizer captures semantic relationships across heterogeneous graphs to support adaptation under heterogeneity shifts.
The Mixture-of-Thought instruction augmentation paradigm generates diverse instructions to address data scarcity.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The framework is reported to learn from arbitrary heterogeneous graphs without downstream-dataset fine-tuning.
Comprehensive evaluations in various settings are reported to show exceptional generalization performance exceeding current leading benchmarks.
The model implementation and accompanying details are reported as openly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Heterogeneous graph learning models complex relational semantics, and recent HGNNs use relation-aware message functions and aggregation rules.
Existing frameworks generalize poorly across diverse datasets, partly because they pre-train and fine-tune on the same dataset.
HiGPT applies heterogeneous graph instruction tuning to adapt across downstream tasks and distribution shifts.
The framework combines an in-context heterogeneous graph tokenizer, heterogeneity-aware graph instructions, and Mixture-of-Thought augmentation.
The authors report strong generalization results across various evaluation settings and open-source implementation.

source_observation.claim: The framework uses in-context tokenization and graph instructions to represent semantic relationships and relation heterogeneity across graphs.

interpretation.claim: Explicitly representing heterogeneous graph semantics may support transfer across graphs with different node and relation distributions.

application.claim: For cross-dataset graph learning, consider reusable semantic tokenization and instruction-based adaptation before adding dataset-specific fine-tuning.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach works for particular graph domains, tasks, or shift magnitudes.

unknowns: No dataset names, task details, metrics, or numerical results are provided.
The abstract does not specify the model architecture, training data scale, or evaluation protocol.
